questions.q: What is the recommended order for diagnosing "the daily load didn't run" in a Snowpipe -> Stream -> Task pipeline?
options: Pipe (did the file load), then Stream (did it capture a change), then Task (did it run/succeed), then Table (did the result land)
Jump straight to assuming the Task is broken and rewrite it
Check the downstream table first and ignore everything upstream
There is no useful order — check everything simultaneously at random
questions.explain: Walking the chain from the beginning (pipe) to the end (table), in order, finds the actual break faster than guessing which link failed.

questions.q: What does SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA returning FALSE mean, when Step 1 confirms rows clearly loaded?
options: The stream itself is the likely problem — often already consumed by an earlier run, or recreated and lost its offset
The warehouse is out of credits
The file format was misconfigured
The task definitely has a syntax error
questions.explain: If rows loaded but the stream shows no data, the stream itself — not the file load — is the point to investigate.

questions.q: In TASK_HISTORY, what does a state of SKIPPED mean, as opposed to FAILED?
options: The task's WHEN condition (often tied to SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA) evaluated false, so the task didn't run at all — it isn't a broken task
SKIPPED and FAILED mean exactly the same thing
The task ran twice by mistake
The warehouse was deleted
questions.explain: SKIPPED indicates the task's WHEN condition was false, which is a normal, working outcome one link back (often an empty stream) — not the same as a real failure.

questions.q: Which Snowflake functions/table functions does this lesson chain together to diagnose the pipeline end to end?
options: SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS / COPY_HISTORY, SYSTEM$STREAM_HAS_DATA, and TASK_HISTORY
Only SHOW WAREHOUSES
Only SCD Type 2 merge logic
Only Power BI's refresh history
questions.explain: The chain uses pipe status/copy history for the load step, stream-has-data for the change-capture step, and task history for the scheduled-processing step.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize checking the chain in order rather than jumping to conclusions?
options: Because a string of SKIPPED task runs, for example, is fully explained by an earlier stalled link (an empty stream), not a broken task — checking in order avoids fixing the wrong thing
Because Snowflake requires queries to run in a specific numbered sequence
Because SQL syntax requires it
Because it reduces warehouse credit costs
questions.explain: Symptoms downstream (like SKIPPED tasks) are often consistent with, and explained by, a problem one or more links earlier — order-checking turns a vague symptom into a specific root cause.
